name: Brazilian tan / spray tan to even skin
lead: Spray tanning is a sunless tanning method in which a dihydroxyacetone (DHA) solution is applied to the skin to produce a temporary bronze color, used in appearance communities to even out skin tone. DHA reacts with amino acids in the dead outer skin layer rather than acting as a dye [2].

A 2005 review described DHA as the only sunless tanning ingredient approved by the FDA and described spray-on products as delivering the formulation evenly to give a full-body tan without ultraviolet exposure [1].
infobox: DHA approved for external use only

paras: DHA is typically used at about 3 to 5 percent and produces color through a Maillard-type reaction in the outer skin; the color fades as skin sheds over days [2]. Application can be in a booth, by an airbrush technician, or at home [1].

Wikipedia credits Eva Wittgenstein with the 1950s discovery of DHA's skin-coloring effect and lists early products Man-Tan (1959) and Coppertone's QT (1960); automated spray booths spread from the late 1990s [2].

The FDA approves DHA for external application only and not for the eyes, lips, mucous membranes or inhalation, and notes that all-over spray booths can make those exposures hard to avoid [2]. Wikipedia also reports studies on free-radical formation under sun exposure after DHA application and contact dermatitis, and notes that a 2010 European Commission opinion found spray tanning posed no risk but was criticized for relying on unpublished industry-linked studies [2]. A tan from DHA provides no UV protection [2].
No studies found examining spray tans specifically for evening skin tone in looksmaxxing contexts. A 2005 review described the technology and formulations [1].

timeline.event: Man-Tan, an early commercial DHA self-tanner, is released [2].

card.summary: A DHA-based temporary skin color applied by spray to even out tone; lasts about a week and offers no UV protection.
card.note: FDA approves DHA for external use only, not inhalation or mucous membranes.

quick.overview:
A spray tan applies DHA to temporarily color the skin and give a more even bronze look without UV exposure.

Results fade over several days as the outer skin sheds.
quick.mechanism: DHA reacts with amino acids in the dead outer layer of skin to produce brown color.
quick.risks: The FDA approves DHA for external use only; contact dermatitis and inhalation concerns are reported, and the tan does not protect against UV.
